abstract: Consider a model with two types of jobs. The profitability of promoting a worker to a fast-track job depends not only on his or her observable talent, but also on incontractible effort. We investigate whether self-fulfilling expectations may lead to women meeting tougher promotion standards than men. If employers expect women to do more household work than men and by that exert less effort in the paid job, the more talented she must be to make promotion profitable. Moreover, specialization in the family will then make women do most of the household work. Such self-fulfilling prophecies can be broken: Both affirmative action and family policy can make women spend more effort in the market, which can lead the economy to a non-discriminatory equilibrium. However, we find that it is unlikely that temporary policy can move the economy to a symmetric equilibrium; policy must be made permanent. Anti-discrimination policy need not enhance efficiency, and from a distribution viewpoint this is a policy with both winners and losers.
abstract_zh: 考虑一个包含两类工作的模型。将员工晋升至快速通道职位的盈利性不仅取决于其可观测的天赋，还取决于不可契约化的努力程度。我们探究自我实现的预期是否会导致女性面临比男性更严苛的晋升标准。若雇主预期女性比男性承担更多家务劳动，从而在职场中付出更少努力，则女性必须拥有更高天赋才能使晋升有利可图。此外，家庭内部的专业化分工将导致女性承担大部分家务劳动。这种自我实现的预言可以被打破：平权行动与家庭政策均能促使女性在劳动力市场投入更多努力，从而引导经济走向无歧视均衡。然而我们发现，临时性政策难以推动经济达到对称均衡，政策必须具有持续性。反歧视政策未必能提升效率，从分配视角看，这类政策既会产生受益者也会产生受损者。
title: Mommy Tracks and Public Policy: On Self-Fulfilling Prophecies and Gender Gaps in Promotion
title_zh: 母亲职业轨迹与公共政策：论自我实现预言与晋升中的性别差距
